title: Hanlon's Razor
coreMove: Check ordinary error before assigning hostile intent, while preserving the evidence that would change the call.
sourcePressure: Frozen support is moderate and narrow through official model reference and table-of-contents identity. The safe floor is to avoid rushing to malice when ignorance, confusion, or ordinary error may explain enough, while clearly preserving accountability when real malice is supported.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version excuses harmful behavior or tells the reader never to suspect malice.

sourceAnchors.name: Hanlon's razor
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen source supports Hanlon's razor as a Volume 1 model and authorizes a narrow paraphrase: do not rush to malice when ordinary error may explain enough, but do not deny real malice
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Check the ordinary mistake first, not because harm is harmless, but because the first story your anger writes may be too expensive.

counterintuition: assume good intent no matter what

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a homeowner whose neighbor keeps blocking a shared driveway
exampleSpecs.stakes: a hostile confrontation could escalate a problem caused by a confusing property line
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Natalie checks the faded driveway marker and old survey before accusing the neighbor of deliberate disrespect
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a faded yellow property marker half-buried in gravel

exampleSpecs.audience: a charge nurse reacting to a repeated mislabeled tray
exampleSpecs.stakes: patient safety needs action, but blame may land before the process error is found
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sean traces the mislabeled tray to two nearly identical shelf bins before deciding whether discipline or system repair comes first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two white medication bins with labels peeling at the same corner

exampleSpecs.audience: a freelancer who believes a client is stalling payment
exampleSpecs.stakes: a relationship may be damaged if a portal error explains the missing approval
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Valeria asks for the approval screenshot and discovers the invoice is stuck under the wrong purchase-order field before sending the angry email
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an unpaid invoice tab open beside a drafted angry email

exampleSpecs.audience: a tenant convinced the building manager ignores repairs
exampleSpecs.stakes: the alarm must be fixed while the cause of the silence is still unknown
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Nils checks the maintenance queue and finds the request filed under the wrong unit, then still sets a deadline for repair
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a chirping smoke alarm balanced on a hallway radiator cover

exampleSpecs.audience: a parent whose child was left off the tournament roster
exampleSpecs.stakes: the parent may accuse the coach before checking whether a registration field failed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ada compares the roster export with the payment receipt and finds the software dropped late registrations, then asks for correction without inventing intent
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a roster printout creased beside a muddy cleat bag

exampleSpecs.audience: someone angry after being left waiting at a train station
exampleSpecs.stakes: the response must protect trust without turning a phone failure into a character trial
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Zoe check the missed-call log and dead phone before deciding whether the pattern is ordinary error or a deeper reliability problem
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a station clock reflected in a dark phone screen

skillTargets: preserve accountability when evidence supports malice
choose a response that gathers facts without escalating prematurely

tryThisNowSpec: For one irritation, write two ordinary-error explanations and the evidence that would make you treat it as intentional instead.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
